mechanisms.duplicates_or_dead: The calibrated fusion policy (crates/adaptive-transport/src/fusion_policy.rs) is the alternative FEC-decision authority and SILENCES this gate when enabled; it has NO structure/burst feature (FusionObservation fields at fusion_policy.rs:84-97 are inputs + rtt_sample_count + telemetry_age + converged + fec_actuation_available + deadline_over_srtt_permille), so enabling it deletes the burst/random distinction entirely.

mechanisms.duplicates_or_dead: The transition-probability estimator (burst_delta_ppm) is the ONLY structural loss signal in the product. It answers 'are losses correlated?' but not 'how long is a burst?', so the §7/§8 questions that need burst length (interleaving depth, whether a burst exceeds r) cannot be asked.
mechanisms.feature_off_behavior: The FEC profile/level is chosen from loss RATE (fuzzy fec_med/fec_high, or gate_level, or the BurstFusion margin formula) plus a binary correlated/uncorrelated flag — never from burst length.

crates/adaptive-transport/src/sender.rs:3719-3733 (BurstFusion level formula uses loss_ppm × 3/2 only — no burst-length term)
mechanisms.notes: The gap matters concretely for K-FEC-NEG-1: deciding whether a burst EXCEEDS r (the criterion that makes closing FEC the right answer) requires burst length, which the product does not measure. The current burst branch closes FEC on correlation alone, regardless of whether the burst is within or beyond r.

open_questions: Which lane actually produced the parity observed in reports/guard-check-v2/iid50/adaptive (tx.fec = 1104/736/2208/1104 B in 4/6 reps)? The arm name contains 'fec-adaptive' but not '-risk', so by crates/bench/src/kama_product.rs:186-190 the speculative lane should be OFF and the structure gate should be the only source — consistent with the Q18 IID branch firing. This cannot be settled from out.jsonl because the bench does not print fec_arbiter_reasons per rep in a machine-readable field; the KP-CLIENT arb= value is in the .err files, which I did not parse. Confirmable by grepping 'arb=' in reports/guard-check-v2/*/adaptive/rep*/c.err.

Does the shipped Q18Iid branch ever fire on prior alone in a REAL netem run (n10+n11 == 0 while loss_windowed_ppm >= 100_000)? The mechanism is proven in tests (crates/adaptive-transport/tests/structure_gate_fec.rs:268-306) and admitted in code (sender.rs:3676-3695), but the counters that would show it (FateWindowDiag n00/n01/n10/n11) are carried to ClientStats and never printed by the bench, so no in-tree netem run can answer it.

reports/burst-reproof-v1 is a frozen pre-registration (PRE-REGISTRATION.md, 2026-08-26) whose out/ directory contains raw per-rep packet captures for 3 profiles x 10 reps x 4 arms but NO out.jsonl result rows and NO FINAL-REPORT.md, and the whole out/ tree is untracked in git. Was the campaign completed and left unanalysed, aborted, or is the analysis pending? Its decision rule (NOT-WORSE / STILL-WORSE / INCONCLUSIVE) is unexecuted, so the P0 fix has never been re-validated against quinn as the pre-registration required.

reports/guard-check-v1 and -v2 are untracked working data with no PRE-REGISTRATION and no closure document, yet they are the only in-tree netem measurements of the BurstFusion arm through the product runtime. Are they intended as evidence, or as exploratory diagnosis? Under the repo's own frozen-experiment governance they cannot support a default flip either way.

Whether emergency (RecoverFwd) is ever entered in the netem campaigns cannot be determined from any in-tree artifact: sender.rs:5980 last_recovery() and :5985 emergency_level() have zero product/bench consumers, and ClientStats.fate.sender_state is a closing-time snapshot only. So the whole §11 cluster's activation rate in measured runs is unobservable.

Sender::new hardcodes Framing::Tiny at sender.rs:3746, which makes the §11 segment-block branch unreachable. Was that a deliberate v1 scope decision (tiny/messaging framing only) or an oversight? No comment or design note in-tree states it, and the §16 TV-EMERGENCY conformance vector (engine-spec:954-956) explicitly requires framing-differentiated behaviour.

crates/client-core/examples/fec_arm_compare.rs:388-392 prints diag_gate_outcomes columns under headers ending in 'peak_ppm', but g[6] is GateOutcome::BlockedPreConverge (sender.rs:286), not a peak ppm value — the last column label is wrong. Cosmetic and confined to a diagnostic example, but it would misread any PreConverge-blocked run.

Neither transport authority (specs/adaptive-transport-engine-spec.md §8.4/§15, specs/transport-layer-tdd.md §5.1/§5.3) contains any loss-STRUCTURE axis, and the §4.4.2 benchmark matrix (transport-layer-tdd.md:270-276) sweeps loss as IID percentages with only 'burst-jitter' on the jitter axis — no burst-loss profile. The GE burst profiles actually used (h3a/b/c, reports/burst-reproof-v1/manifest-h3.jsonl) are therefore harness extensions outside the pre-declared §4.4 matrix. Should §4.4.2 be amended to declare the burst-loss axis, or are these cells formally exploratory?

specs/fec-core-tdd-v3.0.md:394-395 (K-FEC-NEG-1) requires a demonstration that FEC closes or splits in burst-exceeding-r regimes. The product closes FEC on CORRELATION (burst_delta > 50k), not on burst-vs-r comparison, and no burst-length estimator exists. Is the correlation proxy accepted as satisfying K-FEC-NEG-1, or does the criterion require the missing burst_p95 signal?
